current_focus.summary: How the courier finds plugins, what its two doors look like, its limits, and how a store installs it.

decisions.choice: Each taking part plugin offers private POST routes courier/outbox and courier/inbox. Once a run, the courier asks each inbox what it wants (sender, topic) and its bookmark, asks the sender's outbox for news since that bookmark, and hands the batch to the inbox with the new bookmark. The receiver keeps its bookmark and ignores item ids it already has; the courier keeps nothing. Every door refuses a call that carries a person, because EmDash lets an outside request reach a private route only as a signed-in person and the courier calls with none.

decisions.question: How do plugins hand news to each other through the courier, and who keeps track of how far delivery got?

decisions.choice: One handoff carries 50 items unless the receiver asks for up to 100, never more; one run makes at most 20 handoffs; one item is at most 8 KB; one receiver wants at most 20 topics.

history.choice: At most 50 items per handoff, 20 handoffs per run, 8 KB per item and 20 wanted topics per receiver. A run stops at its limit and the next run, about a minute later, carries the rest.

decisions.question: How much does one courier run carry?
decisions.rationale: The owner approved on 22 Nov 2026. Shopify's REST API pages 50 records by default; EmDash plugin storage reads give 50 by default and 100 at most, so a 100-item handoff is one read; WordPress runs timed jobs at most once every 60 seconds.

decisions.choice: Package @dinkuskit/courier, installed from a GitHub tag. Only Cloudflare stores run it: the store's existing once-a-minute timer calls courierScheduled() from the Worker's scheduled() handler, reaching EmDash through withEmDashRuntime, so nobody needs to be signed in. The Node visit hook is removed; how a self-hosted Node store runs the courier is decided when self-hosting is supported. A receiving plugin's admin page shows when the courier last came, or that it is missing.

history.choice: Package @dinkuskit/courier, installed from a GitHub tag. On Cloudflare the store's once-a-minute timer runs it from the Worker's scheduled() handler; on Node the site's middleware starts a run on any visit at most once a minute, after the page. Both reach EmDash through withEmDashRuntime, so nobody needs to be signed in. A receiving plugin's admin page shows when the courier last came, or that it is missing.

decisions.question: How does a store run the courier?
decisions.rationale: The owner approved on 22 Nov 2026: every store today runs on Cloudflare, where the template's timer already fires each minute, so the courier is one more line on it at no extra cost; self-hosting is parked, so the Node path waits for it.

decisions.choice: Courier reads EmDash's authoritative _plugin_state.registry_slug for active source='registry' installs (never self-reported by plugins) and resolves a unique matching outbox; if more than one installed outbox matches a requested name, courier fails closed with SENDER_AMBIGUOUS; stores may also pass an explicit options.senders map to courierScheduled/runCourier to pin a specific outbox id (failing closed as SENDER_MISSING if absent); deliver keeps the receiver's requested from name so bookmark keys stay stable.
